problem_text:
A logistics coordinator is tasked with assembling a shipment of specialized equipment to maximize total utility score while adhering to the cargo plane's maximum payload limit.

The equipment units available are:
* Unit A: mass 8 tons, utility 274 credits
* Unit B: mass 23 tons, utility 181 credits
* Unit C: mass 28 tons, utility 189 credits
* Unit D: mass 15 tons, utility 67 credits
* Unit E: mass 27 tons, utility 258 credits
* Unit F: mass 47 tons, utility 272 credits
* Unit G: mass 6 tons, utility 249 credits
* Unit H: mass 20 tons, utility 25 credits
* Unit I: mass 22 tons, utility 285 credits
* Unit J: mass 31 tons, utility 70 credits
* Unit K: mass 43 tons, utility 297 credits
* Unit L: mass 47 tons, utility 163 credits
* Unit M: mass 7 tons, utility 200 credits
* Unit N: mass 3 tons, utility 102 credits
* Unit O: mass 20 tons, utility 103 credits
* Unit P: mass 22 tons, utility 254 credits
* Unit Q: mass 15 tons, utility 204 credits
* Unit R: mass 22 tons, utility 285 credits
* Unit S: mass 1 ton, utility 200 credits
* Unit T: mass 22 tons, utility 300 credits
* Unit U: mass 29 tons, utility 114 credits
* Unit V: mass 30 tons, utility 223 credits
* Unit W: mass 37 tons, utility 171 credits
* Unit X: mass 28 tons, utility 229 credits
* Unit Y: mass 31 tons, utility 107 credits
* Unit Z: mass 11 tons, utility 255 credits

Furthermore, due to compatibility protocols, exactly one of Unit A and Unit B must be included in the shipment.

If Unit C is selected, the effective payload capacity of the aircraft is diminished by 10 tons.
The aircraft's maximum allowable payload is 416 tons. The coordinator must determine which units to load.
